3 US Presidential Election Polling via Frequentist Methods

We will soon turn our attention back to our second motivational example, that of US Presidential election polling, but first we must do some revision and define our notation.

3.1 Random Variables, Expectation & Variance: Revision and Notation

3.1.1 Discrete Random Variables

  • •

    A discrete random variable X is a variable which can take a finite (or countable) set of different numerical values x1,x2,⋯∈𝒳, according to the different possible outcomes of an experiment or random phenomenon.

  • •

    We denote the probability mass function (p.m.f), also called the probability function (p.f.) (see for example DeGroot & Schervish), as

    f⁢(x)=P⁢(X=x),for all⁢x∈𝒳. (5)
  • •

    Note that sometimes the probability mass function is denoted p⁢(x), but it will be convenient for us to use f⁢(x) to be more in alignment with the continuous case.

Example: Discrete Random Variables

Possible values, x 0 1 2 3 4 5
Probabilities, P⁢(X=x) 0.33 0.41 0.20 0.05 0.01 0.00

Since the possible values for X are exhaustive and mutually exclusive, the probability that X takes one of the values within a specific set can be calculated using the addition law for disjoint events. For example:

P⁢(X∈{1,3})=P⁢(X=1⁢or⁢X=3)=P⁢(X=1)+P⁢(X=3)=0.41+ 0.05=0.46
  • •

    Often, a discrete random variable has a distribution that depends on an external parameter.

Definition: The Poisson Distribution

The Poisson distribution depends on the parameter λ. We write X∼P⁢o⁢(λ) and denote its p.m.f. as

f⁢(x|λ)=P⁢(X=x)={e−λ⁢λxx!for⁢x=0,1,2,…0otherwise. (6)
  • •

    Note the new notation when specifying a specific probability distribution above: f⁢(x|λ), to be read as “f of x given λ”. This is needed because in order for us to calculate the probability mass function for the Poisson distribution we need to be told (i.e. given) the value of λ. If λ was uncertain, which it will be later in the course, then this would affect our p.m.f of X, hence we cannot just use the notation f⁢(x) here.

  • •

    This will also allow us to use Bayes theorem with these objects too!
